items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 12 (statements; injuries from the Oct 10 strike)
items.source_name: Philippine Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) via screencap.com.ph
items.summary: The Philippine Department of Migrant Workers confirmed on Monday that 4 Filipino overseas workers were injured in the Oct 10 Houthi missile strike on King Khalid International Airport, with 3 of them in hospital intensive care in Riyadh. OWWA administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan said at least 30 Filipinos were stranded in Riyadh (20 in DMW-OWWA sponsored hotel accommodations, 7 picked up by local relatives, 2 in-transit seafarers in airline-provided lodging); DMW secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said 94 Manila-bound and transit OFWs were diverted to Jeddah, and 37 workers stranded at Manila's NAIA terminals are receiving OWWA assistance. Cacdac confirmed there is no deployment ban on Saudi Arabia for now.
items.title: Philippines confirms 4 Filipino OFWs injured in Oct 10 Riyadh airport strike (3 in ICU); 30 stranded, 94 diverted to Jeddah

items.summary: A TV5 News graphic posted on the News5 Facebook page (dated Oct 13, using a Reuters photo of the Riyadh airport fire) claims the number of Filipinos injured in the Riyadh airport attack has risen to 7. This conflicts with the Philippine DMW's confirmed figure of 4 (3 in ICU) and could not be corroborated; treat as unverified.
items.title: TV5 graphic claims Filipino injuries in Riyadh airport attack rose to 7 — conflicts with DMW's confirmed 4
